messages:
pagerduty-bot: INCIDENT CREATED · CRITICAL · runtime-engine crashloop on pool-gpu-p3-12 (auto-escalation to oncall) :rotating_light:

alice.engineering: I'm seeing a node in pool-gpu-p3-12 go into CrashLoopBackOff. Containers restart every ~12s and the app logs show a segfault coming from the runtime core. Repro rate ~100% for requests that trigger the quantized path.

bob_oncall: Confirmed. k8s events: `Back-off restarting failed container` + pod keep restarting. Quick logs: 
```
# runtime stderr
[2026-03-15T01:12:07Z] runtime: segfault at 0x0 ip 0x7f8b2f4a9e3c sp 0x7ffcf1a2f8f0
# fused_kernel.cu:123
# Traceback (most recent call last):
#   ...
# SIGSEGV (Segmentation fault)
```

carol_sre: Also seeing kernel messages on the node intermittently: `NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:66:00): 13, pid 13890` and a `device-side assert` in CUDA logs for some processes. Could be a bad kernel/kernel-compat or driver issue. Node appears to have flapped once (node became NotReady for ~30s).

dave_ml_runtime: From the trace + repro pattern this smells like our fused TensorRT kernel when running int8 / fused attention. We had a similar class of failures in 2025 with quant path. Quick mitigation options: disable fused kernels (env var), fallback to non-TRT runtime, or roll back to previous runtime image (v2.1.3) which was stable.

alice.engineering: What is easiest to push right now? We have customer traffic routed to this pool (Dedicated tenants A and B). Impact: ~5% error rate and some requests stuck in retry loops.

bob_oncall: Short plan: 1) route new traffic away from pool-gpu-p3-12 2) apply env override to disable fused kernels on remaining nodes in pool 3) redeploy or restart pods on pool to pick up change.

carol_sre: I'll start a partial drain on the most flaky node (node-gpu-17) and cordon it: `kubectl cordon node-gpu-17 && kubectl drain node-gpu-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force` to avoid further customer impact.

dave_ml_runtime: To disable fused kernels at runtime (non-invasive) you can set: `REDWOOD_RUNTIME_DISABLE_FUSED=true` or `REDWOOD_RUNTIME_TRT_FALLBACK=1` depending on deployment. For k8s deploy: 
```
kubectl -n inference set env deploy/runtime REDWOOD_RUNTIME_DISABLE_FUSED=true --record
kubectl rollout restart deploy/runtime
```
This avoids a full image rollback and should bypass the TensorRT fused path. 

alice.engineering: Applying the env now to one canary pod in pool-gpu-p3-12 to test.

bob_oncall: While that's running, I'm increasing max core dumps retention and capturing a coredump for offline analysis: `echo 1 > /proc/sys/kernel/core_uses_pid` and configuring `coredumpctl` to collect. Also attaching gdb to the crash image once we have the dump.

erin_support: I've opened a customer impact ticket for Dedicated tenants A & B, notifying monitored SLAs. Adding customer-facing blurb: "We're investigating an internal inference runtime issue causing intermittent errors; mitigation in progress. No data loss. Updates every 30m."

dave_ml_runtime: Canary result: the canary with `REDWOOD_RUNTIME_DISABLE_FUSED=true` is stable -> no segfaults for 15m under comparable load. Good sign. We should roll the env to the rest of the pool.

carol_sre: Rolling env to the pool now (staged): `kubectl -n inference patch deployment runtime -p '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"rerun":"disable-fused-316245"}}}}}'` then `kubectl -n inference set env deploy/runtime REDWOOD_RUNTIME_DISABLE_FUSED=true`. Watching for pod restarts.

alice.engineering: After rolling, crashloops stopped on previously affected pods. Node flaps have subsided. Latency is slightly higher for fused-replaced code paths but error rate falls to <0.5%.

bob_oncall: Notifying infra: we should still collect artifacts and look into why the TRT fused kernel caused SIGSEGV. Possible causes: 1) corrupted kernel image on node after recent kernel/driver update 2) bad model that triggers OOB memory access with int8 tensors 3) race in our fused launch.

dave_ml_runtime: Agreed — will run targeted regression tests with quantized models and also run quick binary diff against v2.1.3 -> v2.1.4 runtime to find introduced fused-kernel changes. I'll spin up an isolated repro job with the same model and dataset.

erin_support: Customer comms updated: informing tenants A & B that traffic has been rerouted away from affected pool, and temporary mitigation applied. ETA for a technical postmortem: 48 hours.

carol_sre: Handoff: bob_oncall -> carol_sre (oncall rotation in 40m). bob, please include the coredump location and the canary pod id in the handoff.

bob_oncall: coredump saved to /var/crash/node-gpu-17/runtime-core-316245.dmp, uploaded to internal-storage at `s3://redwood-incident-dumps/3162456789/`. Canary pod: `runtime-5b7f9d8c4b-tyz2p`. Leaving notes in PagerDuty, switching to follow mode. :white_check_mark:

alice.engineering: Will follow up with a minimal repro and high-priority PR to add a runtime safety check to the fused kernel parameters (bounds checks).

dave_ml_runtime: Also adding a temporary guard in the runtime to disable int8 fused launches unless a flag is present and to emit extra sanity logs. Won't ship to customers until PR review.

erin_support: I'll schedule the initial customer update for +30m and copy SRE/Eng.

carol_sre: I'm taking the oncall. Current status: mitigation applied (env var), traffic rerouted, crashlooping pods recovered. Action items for follow-up: collect deeper logs, reproduce in staging, plan rollback if regression identified, postmortem. Marking incident active -> mitigated.

bob_oncall: Thanks team. Leaving this in your queue carol. I'll be reachable if anything flips back.

carol_sre: copying incident thread to #postmortems and assigning P0 to dave_ml_runtime + alice.engineering for a 48h postmortem.

pagerduty-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE · mitigated -> followup required. Primary mitigation: disabled fused kernels (REDWOOD_RUNTIME_DISABLE_FUSED=true) and routed traffic away from pool-gpu-p3-12.
